Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

rendered.content:
<system-reminder>
The following MCP servers require authentication before their tools can be used:
plugin:marketing:ahrefs
plugin:marketing:amplitude
plugin:marketing:amplitude-eu
plugin:marketing:canva
plugin:marketing:figma
plugin:marketing:hubspot
plugin:marketing:klaviyo
plugin:marketing:notion
plugin:marketing:similarweb
plugin:marketing:slack
plugin:marketing:supermetrics

Claude cannot start the OAuth flow itself. If the user's request depends on one of these servers (even if they didn't name it explicitly), or they ask about it, tell them that it needs to be authorized — for claude.ai connectors, via their claude.ai connector settings; for other servers, via /mcp — and that the capability is unavailable until they do. Otherwise carry on with the request and do not mention these servers. Do not ask the user for authorization codes, tokens, or callback URLs.
</system-reminder>

## 1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai .../artifact/... link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{...}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

The registry's original source and comments are retained under
`src/components/dither-kit`. These source files were adapted to Notary: blue
palette, explicit observed axis ticks, step sampling for recorded line trends,
no decorative stars, and data receipts with unknown values preserved. Canvas
fills are decorative; measured values remain available as text and accessible
chart descriptions. Gradients use a static blue wash over a dark blue surface.
The Dither Kit docs credit Evil Charts as the original visual inspiration.

New dependencies are exact: motion 14.1.0, d3-scale 4.0.2, d3-shape 3.2.0,

## Read-only audit of packages/web after 409fd51

I edited nothing and ran no builds or tests. Line numbers refer to the current working tree.

### Verified issues

| Sev | File:line | Bug | Failure scenario | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **High** (fixture leak) | `src/components/landing/replay.ts:30-41`, `FeatureMinis.tsx:40-90` (the `memo` caches and `loadRevocation` at :73), `HowArt.tsx:27-49` | The landing's data caches are keyed only by the `ReplaySource`, and `fixturesInLocation()` is read once, on the first call. The source lives in `DataSourceProvider` above the router, so it survives client-side navigation. | Open `/?fixtures=1`, which caches the fixture pair. Click "Open dashboard" (`Nav.tsx:75` / `Hero.tsx:117`, a plain `/app` link that drops the flag). Then click the sidebar brand link (`Sidebar.tsx:57`, `to="/"`). The default landing now shows fixture data in Hero, the feature minis, How it works and the chat showcase. `Below`/Proof recomputes on each mount and shows real runs, so one page mixes fixture and real data. | Key the caches by `(source, fixtures)`, e.g. a `Map<boolean, Promise>` inside the WeakMap entry, or pass the flag in explicitly. |
| **High** (CLAUDE.md banner rule) | `landing-data.ts:567-574` (`EVALUATION_TAG`), `Hero.tsx:136`, `Proof.tsx:158`; nothing at all in `FeatureMinis.tsx`, `HowArt.tsx`, `ChatShowcase.tsx`/`chat-turn.ts` | Fixture data on the landing never shows the required "Fixture data — simulated APIs, not a live run" text. Two frames get a small "Evaluation suite" tag. The certificate card, held card, revocation, How it works art and chat showcase show `sample:true` data with no disclosure. `BANNED_WORDS` forbids the word "fixture" on the landing. | `/?fixtures=1`, and also the leak in the row above. | Show `FixtureNote` (or the `FIXTURE_BANNER` text) whenever the landing renders `sample:true` data, and exempt that string from `BANNED_RE`. |
| **Med** (mixing) | `pages/approvals/model.ts:215-222`, `components/shell/status.tsx:110-111` | In live mode the server's real pending approvals are always listed. A pending item whose bundle is not in the visible cohort has `bundle === undefined`, so it is not dropped as sample. The sidebar badge also skips the visible-run filter when `mode === "live"`. | Live `notary serve` with `?fixtures=1`: the Approvals page lists real, approvable pending money actions next to fixture history, under the fixture banner. The badge counts real items in the fixture view. | In `buildDesk`, keep only pending and decided items whose `runId` is in `bundles`, or hide pending when `fixtures` is on. Apply the `visibleIds` filter in live mode too. |
| **High** (crash, pre-existing, live mode) | `pages/approvals/index.tsx:38,91,96`, with `AppShell.tsx:126` | `Gate` lets a still-running `missingRunId` through, but `ApprovalsPage` does `bundle!` and then `selected.decisions` / `selected.runId`. | Live mode: start a run (RunPage sets `?run=<id>`), then load `/app/approvals?run=<id>` while the catalog lists it as running (page reload or a shared link). Result: TypeError and a blank app. | Handle `!bundle` in ApprovalsPage, or have Gate send gated routes without a bundle to an "in progress" state. |
| Med | `pages/incidents/model.ts:127-134`, `IncidentsPage.tsx:260-264` | "Matches the published bundle" only compares `file.bundleHash` with the index entry's `contentHash`. It never uses the browser-recomputed bundle hash. | If a bundle JSON is tampered with but `index.json` is not, every other page shows "Runs withheld" while Incidents shows a green "Matches the published bundle". | Tie to `useData().bundles` (already hash-verified), or reword the pill to "Listed in the bundle index". |
| Low-Med | `pages/incidents/model.ts:140,183` | `shown` is true for `unpublished` and `unchecked` runs, so their incidents count in the headline stats. | The stats mix verified and unverified runs with nothing marking which is which. | Count only `verified` runs in the stats, or label the unverified share. |
| Low-Med | `data/incidents.ts:57-69` | The real and fixture incidents files are fetched and parsed together, and either one throwing fails the whole load. | A malformed `incidents/fixture/index.json` withholds the real incidents in the default view, which never shows fixtures. | Parse only the cohort being viewed, or isolate errors per file. |
| Med (a11y) | `src/docs/DocsPage.tsx:209-216` with `hook-sidebar.tsx:258-263` | A table-of-contents click calls `preventDefault()` and `scrollIntoView` but never moves focus. On phones it also closes the `<details>` that holds the focused link. | Keyboard or screen-reader users: the next Tab goes to the next contents item, not into the section. On mobile, focus lands on a hidden element. | Give sections `tabIndex={-1}`, call `el.focus({preventScroll:true})`, and close the details only after focus has moved. |
| Low (a11y) | `hook-sidebar.tsx:191`, `DocsPage.tsx:232,245` | `labelId` is built from the label text, and `TocGroups` renders twice (desktop sidebar and compact contents). | Duplicate `id="hook-sidebar-<group>"` values, so `aria-labelledby` points at duplicate ids (axe duplicate-id-aria). | Use `useId()`. |
| Med (tooling) | `scripts/visual-check.mjs:17-36,44-52,75,80,85`; `scripts/screenshots.mjs:18-29,52-56` | Both scripts open fixture runs via `?run=demo-…` without `?fixtures=1`, which now gives "Run … is not published". visual-check also expects `data-theme="dark"`, `.ui-band-sky` (no longer rendered), 4 sidebar items (there are 6) and h1 "Notary Chat". screenshots.mjs still captures a "dark" pass. | `check:visual` fails on every page, and screenshots are of error pages. | Add `&fixtures=1`, drop the dark matrix and the sky-band/4-item assertions, and add Business and Incidents. |
| Low | `packages/web/package.json:20` | `@tanstack/react-virtual` 3.14.13 is still a dependency. Nothing imports it; RunPage used it before 409fd51. | Dead dependency. | Remove it, or reinstate virtualization (see the Transcript note below). |
| Low | `packages/web/docs/CREDITS.md:71-74,84` | It says "motion 14.1.0, d3-scale 4.0.2, d3-shape…" and points to `src/components/dither-kit`. The repo has motion 13.4.6, no d3 and no dither-kit directory. It also says Transcript uses Hook Sidebar "unmodified", but it uses the adapted file. | Inaccurate attribution and dependency record. | Fix the text. |
| Low | `Transcript.tsx:291`, `pages/chat/chat-tokens.css:2` | Stale comments: "plain (non-virtualized) transcript", and "dark under [data-theme=dark]". | — | Update them. |
| Low | `IncidentsPage.tsx:156` with `AppShell.tsx:163` | The fixture view shows two fixture banners: the shell header note plus `inc-fixture`. | Duplicate disclosure. | Suppress one, as BusinessPage does. |
| Low | `AppShell.tsx:113-115` | The empty check runs before `ungated`, so Business, Incidents and Chat become "No runs" when the cohort has no runs. | `?fixtures=1` with no fixture runs hides Business, which only ever shows real data. | Exempt `business`/`incidents` in `worksWithoutRuns`, or ignore the flag for real-only pages. |
| Low | `App.tsx:20`; dead exports at `Transcript.tsx:296` (`TranscriptRows`, test-only), `links.ts:53` (`MODE_LABEL`), `PageHeader.tsx:72-74` (`SkyBand`/`SkyBandContext` aliases, still used by Chat and the two Certificates pages) | The NotFound link drops `?fixtures=1`. Leftover aliases and exports. | — | `keepView("/app/run")`; delete or rename the aliases and exports. |

### Checked and OK
- **links.ts / catalog.tsx:**
  - `visibleRuns` keeps the cohorts strictly apart, and hidden runs are not even fetched.
  - `groupRuns`, the baseline candidates and `defaultRunId` stay within one cohort.
  - `withRun`, `keepView` and `recordPath` keep `?fixtures=1`; the sidebar, command palette, breadcrumb and incidents filters all go through them.
  - With an empty index, `NoRunsPage` appears and there is no fallback to fixtures.
  - The live server never returns sample runs (`core/src/api/server.ts:28`), so running entries being treated as non-sample is safe.
- **Banner on dashboard pages:** every page uses `PageHeader`, which shows `FixtureNote` when the selected bundle is sample. Business suppresses it on purpose (real data only).
- **Hashes:**
  - Bundles get schema check, recomputed `computeContentHash` and an index-entry match (`verify.ts:110-130`) in both Replay and Live. A failure shows the "Runs withheld" error.
  - Timelines are tied to the verified bundle hash.
  - `economics.json` is zod-checked and hash-recomputed.
  - `incidents` and `entire.json` are zod-validated, but their schemas have no content hash.
- **Core imports:** only `core/src/schema/*` (index, bundle, agents, entire) and `core/src/bundle/hash`. hash.ts only imports schema, with no node: imports.
- **Hardcoded numbers:** none found in Business, Incidents, EntireSection, the landing components or docs/content.tsx.
- **Dependencies:**
  - New: `motion` 13.4.6 (exact). Core: `neatlogs` was changed from `^1.1.26` to exactly `1.1.26`. No root `package.json` change.
  - Caret ranges that predate this commit: `@phosphor-icons/react`, `@radix-ui/react-slot`, `class-variance-authority`, `clsx`, `react`, `tailwind-merge`, `zod`, the devDeps, and core's `@aws-sdk`, `hono`, `commander`.
- **Hook Sidebar:** the full MIT + Commons Clause + Attribution header is present. Visible rareui.com credits are on /docs (`DocsPage.tsx:137-145`) and under the transcript (`Transcript.tsx:793-798`). It uses `useReducedMotion` for the springs, `motion-reduce:` for colour transitions, `aria-current`, and native links and buttons.
- **Reasoning Steps:** the header says it is an original component that mirrors Kobra's API and that Kobra's source was never read. It has `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`, a polite live region, `[data-reduced]` plus `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)` CSS that stops the spin and shimmer, and labelled status glyphs. No a11y bugs found.
- **routes.tsx / main.tsx / App.tsx:** lazy `App` and `DocsPage` have default exports, all 8 routes resolve, redirects are fine. No broken routes found.
- **No orphan files:** every `.ts`, `.tsx` and `.css` file in `src` is imported from somewhere in `src`.

### Transcript performance (`pages/run/Transcript.tsx`)
- **Not virtualized:** every row renders as a Hook Sidebar button, one sidebar per stage, each with a ResizeObserver and two motion rails.
- **Biggest timelines:** 150 events (`bundles/fixture/demo-notarize-dodo.timeline.json`) and 140 (`demo-change-api-notarize-dodo`). The biggest real one has 75 events (`notarize-dodo-20261012T012315Z`). There is no `public/runs` directory.
